examples.question_text: Write $\cos 230^{\circ}$ as a signed ratio of its acute reference angle. Do not evaluate.
The point $P$ lies on the unit circle at an angle of inclination of $300^{\circ}$. Find its exact coordinates.

examples.solution_text:
Sine is negative in Q3; cosine is positive in Q4.

$\begin{aligned}\sin 240^{\circ}&=-\sin 60^{\circ}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\cos 315^{\circ}&=\cos 45^{\circ}\\&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sin 240^{\circ}+\cos 315^{\circ}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\\&=\frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: 230° is in Q3. Its acute reference angle is 230°−180°=50°. Cosine is negative there, so cos 230°=−cos 50°. The diagram's terminal arm and arcs agree.
240°=180°+60° lies in Q3. Applying the quadrant signs to the exact 60° values gives sin 240°=−√3/2, cos 240°=−1/2 and tan 240°=√3. The diagram shows the corresponding 60° reference angle.
315°=360°−45° lies in Q4. Therefore sin 315°=−1/√2, cos 315°=1/√2 and tan 315°=−1. The terminal arm and reference-angle arc match these values.

On the unit circle, P=(cos 300°,sin 300°). The Q4 reference angle is 60°, giving P=(1/2,−√3/2). TikZ places P at (300:1); its perpendicular ends at (0.5,0), and the right-angle marker lies inside the constructed triangle.
sin 240°=−√3/2 and cos 315°=1/√2=√2/2. Their sum is (√2−√3)/2. The bare opening expression has the required phantom equals gutter; no diagram is needed for this arithmetic application.
